text:
RedLine Solutions is hiring a fully remote mid-level C#/.NET developer. We are looking at an early September start date. I'm posting this way ahead of time to try something weird: If you are an interested developer, please do NOT contact me directly. Instead, find someone who will vouch for you and have them send me your resume`. I do NOT need them to write a full-on recommendation--a simple, "Ross was a great developer and fun colleague. You should check him out" will be fine.

1. Please make sure your contact information is on your resume`!

2. We need a developer located within three hours of Pacific timezone.

No, I'm not on some kind of power trip (yet). I just got my fill of automated application spam a long time ago; the tales I could tell. This is my modestly creative attempt to circumvent the AI's. Might be good practice for SkyNet, eh?

We are not looking for a know-it-all. Instead, we desire a "wants to learn it all". We're a small company, but our System Architect / Dev Lead is seriously a unicorn. If he mentors you for a year or two, your career is golden with or without AI. Back in the day, I secretly believed I was one of the best around. Then I worked with Stephen. I've learned a ton from him, and I'm his boss.

We're a small, agile, creative and laid-back team who work hard but value work-life balance. I take great pains to make it so. If you're smart, work hard, and love writing software, ask a friend or former boss to vouch for you and have them send your resume`.

Here's a link to the official job listing:

https://rlsmediastore.blob.core.windows.net/releases/RedLine...

Thanks, Ross W. Lambert, Director of Software Development RedLine Solutions, Inc. https://redlineforproduce.com
